subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw replace the current single chat/agent run deadline with activity-aware idle timeout plus a separate hard cap, and how should that map onto existing `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`?
rationale: The remaining work changes core runtime semantics, may add or reinterpret config/default behavior, and can extend resource usage; the current open PRs do not settle that product contract.

options.title: Define idle timeout plus hard cap
options.body: Adopt the two-budget contract first, then request or review one focused implementation that keeps liveness, hard-stop safety, and timeout messaging aligned.

options.title: Land only slice mitigations
options.body: Review the timeout-notice and subagent-heartbeat PRs independently while keeping this issue open for the broader run-budget design.

options.title: Keep wall-clock semantics
options.body: Treat the current 48-hour default and explicit timeout configuration as sufficient, then narrow this issue to timeout messaging or close it by maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Define idle timeout plus hard cap
recommendation.body: Adopt the two-budget contract first, then request or review one focused implementation that keeps liveness, hard-stop safety, and timeout messaging aligned.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses gateway active-run state, embedded runner liveness, and config policy, and recent history gives steipete the strongest routing signal for that boundary.
